attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his newsletter, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Faithfully gives the year-to-date decline of about a third and the comparison with the broad market.

contract.note: Reading 'a third' as approximate, using the S&P 500 as the market, and measuring price returns to April 4 are ordinary, fair choices. A literal 33.3% reading could change the result.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report: Nvidia closed April 4 down roughly 30% year to date, close to one third.
S&P 500 down 13.7% year to date at the same close. Nvidia's fall was over twice as large.

reviews.rationale: Matching April 4 endpoints show Nvidia down about 30% year to date against 13.7% for the S&P 500. Under the contract's approximate reading, a ~30% fall counts as about a third, and it far exceeds the market's fall.

attribution.note: Marcus's own summary line in his post.

semantics.note: The colloquial 'ain't no GPT-5' is fairly read as: not publicly released as of the post date.

contract.note: Public release under the GPT-5 name is the ordinary reading. The result does not depend on interpretation.

evidence.note: OpenAI's CEO said on April 4, 2025 that GPT-5 would come in a few months, so it was unreleased. This is a company disclosure, but a reliable record of release status.
GPT-5 was introduced August 7, 2025. This is consistent with no release before April 6, but it falls outside the period.

reviews.rationale: Two days before the post, OpenAI's CEO described GPT-5 as months away. Its later launch date of August 7, 2025 confirms it had not been released by April 6, 2025.

attribution.note: Marcus's own concluding assertion, tied to his tariff discussion in the same post.

semantics.note: The firm causal assertion is kept. Earlier in the post Marcus said 'probably', but the summary line is unhedged.

contract.note: Tying the claim to the April 2025 tariff episode follows his own context. Requiring a demonstrated causal chain is reasonable. 'Deep doodoo' has no threshold.

evidence.note: Chatbots gave similar formulas, but actual government use is explicitly unverified.
Lutnick denied using AI. Under the contract a denial alone cannot contradict the claim. It is weak counterevidence.
Documents severe market losses after the tariffs. Says nothing about LLM causation.

reviews.rationale: Harm from the tariffs is documented. But no evidence shows officials relied on LLM output. Only the formulas' similarity is known, against an official denial that is not corroborated. The causal link is neither established nor refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assessment of the current situation and of his earlier predictions.

semantics.note: Keeps every part: GPT-5 level is hard, similar models, essentially no moat, a price war, profits modest at best, and 'exactly where we are'.

contract.note: Scoring the April 2025 state is fair. The evaluator chose the profit population, period and basis because Marcus named none, and the result depends on those choices.

evidence.note: Meta's own post: Behemoth was still training, alongside claimed benchmark gains. Too mixed to settle the claim.
Shows parity between rival providers on reasoning tasks. That is one component; it shows nothing about moats or profits.
OpenAI reports price cuts. This does not establish a price war, the absence of a moat, or profits.

reviews.rationale: The evidence partly bears on similar models and falling prices. Nothing establishes no durable moat, a price war as the cause of the cuts, modest realized profits, or difficulty reaching GPT-5 level. The combined claim cannot be settled from this packet.
